sections.heading: Careers, major choices, SFIA and cloud/data centre development
headingPath: Careers, major choices, SFIA and cloud/data centre development
sections.text:
Possible career directions include:
Analysis and Development: Database Developer, Programmer Analyst, Web/Mobile Developer, Systems Analyst, Software Engineer, Full Stack Developer.
Network Systems and Cybersecurity: Network Operations Specialist, Network and Systems Engineer, System Integration Engineer, Network/Data Administrator, Network/Cloud Infrastructure Engineer, Cybersecurity Analyst/Practitioner, Cybersecurity Architect, Penetration Tester, Risk and Compliance Specialist.
Data Analytics and Enterprise Systems: Data Analyst, ICT Business Analyst, Business Intelligence Analyst, Web Analyst, Data Insights Analyst, Data Scientist, Consulting Analyst.
Project and Support: Project Manager/Administrator, ICT Support Officer, Service Desk Analyst, Technical/Business Systems Support Engineer, ICT Trainer, ICT Consultant.
The course owner reports that the course is being developed to prepare students for cloud and data-centre work in Melbourne's expanding AI data-centre sector. This describes development direction, not a guarantee of a particular unit, employment or internship. Match interests to current configured subject content and major requirements. SFIA is the Skills Framework for the Information Age; alignment is not automatic professional certification, a skills-assessment outcome or a job guarantee.

sections.heading: Applying for Bachelor of IT, ACS accreditation and admissions
headingPath: Applying for Bachelor of IT, ACS accreditation and admissions
sections.text: Apply through the Bachelor of IT registration form, telephone 1300 635 276, or submit the course enquiry form. The ACS accredited-courses directory is the source for current accreditation listings; check the relevant course and intake rather than promising a skills-assessment result. Local admissions categories are recent secondary education (current year or previous two years), VET study, higher education study, and work/life experience (left secondary school more than two years ago without subsequent VET/higher education study). Uncompleted prior study can affect the category. Indigenous applicants are welcomed. Domestic applicants with overseas qualifications should consult credit transfer/RPL guidance. English proficiency and course-specific requirements are on the course page. RPL and advanced related qualifications/work are assessed case by case by academics and, where appropriate, industry experts. Do not decide admission or credit approval in chat.

sections.heading: Enrolled but no Moodle subjects; Student Portal and Student Declaration
headingPath: Enrolled but no Moodle subjects; Student Portal and Student Declaration
sections.text: Teachers may keep Moodle subjects hidden until the first class. If you recently replied to your Student Declaration email, subject enrolment may take a few days to finish. Check the Student Portal to see whether you are enrolled; Moodle visibility is not enrolment confirmation. If subjects are not in Student Portal after a few days, ask Nandini Biskunda, School Administration, to follow up: NandiniBiskunda@melbournepolytechnic.edu.au. If enrolled in Student Portal but the first class has started and Moodle still has no subject, contact the lecturer or administration. Distinguish this from inability to log in. Do not add a Source line.

sections.heading: Orientation: learning resources, email, rooms, assessment and internships
headingPath: Orientation: learning resources, email, rooms, assessment and internships
sections.text: Use your MP email for official teacher/school communications and monitor it regularly. The Student Portal is the starting point for enrolment, results, My Info, library and support. Office 365 is available to students through portal/library instructions. The library offers referencing help, LinkedIn Learning and study support; Studiosity offers after-hours learning advice. Student cards are available via Student Hub. In PE321, P means Preston, E the building, 3 the floor and 21 the room. The Moodle mobile app can provide teacher-message notifications and access to resources. Ask the teacher first about assessments, submission problems or grade concerns, then course administration if unresolved. Special consideration, extensions and reasonable adjustments are distinct processes; use HE-specific guidance and supporting evidence, not VET forms/deadlines applied automatically to a Bachelor student. Capstone is a year-long team project, typically with two or three other students; Software Development and Business Analytics often have external-company projects. Network Security external projects can be harder to source. Actual projects must be confirmed with course staff. Internship support and self-sourced opportunities exist; do not promise placements from a historical success anecdote. Use current configuration for all dates, grades, loads, timetables and SAS awards; the orientation slides contain obsolete grade ranges and Semester 2 dates. Refer international load/attendance/visa questions to International Office rather than deciding visa compliance.

sections.heading: Student Charter and SLAM student life
headingPath: Student Charter and SLAM student life
sections.text: Student Charter: MP commits to industry opportunities, practical learning, teachers who support student potential, help identifying strengths, education and wellbeing support in a safe inclusive environment, and a collaborative community. The charter reflects student feedback and guides staff practice. SLAM (Student Life at Melbourne Polytechnic) runs free events for current students, competitions, music, pop-ups, giveaways and support for student-run activities. Check Student Portal for events. Contact slam@melbournepolytechnic.edu.au.
